208: /// Evaluate all arguments from a call, performing expansions when necessary.

210:     engine_state: &EngineState,
211:     stack: &mut Stack,
212:     call: &Call,
213: ) -> Result<Vec<Spanned<String>>, ShellError> {
214:     let cwd = engine_state.cwd(Some(stack))?;

219:             // glob-expansion, and inner-quotes-removal, in that order.
220:             for arg in eval_argument(engine_state, stack, expr, spread)? {
221:                 for glob_expanded in expand_glob(&arg, &cwd, expr.span)? {
222:                     args.push(glob_expanded.into_spanned(expr.span));
223:                 }
224:             }
225:         } else {
226:             for arg in eval_argument(engine_state, stack, expr, spread)? {
227:                 args.push(arg.into_spanned(expr.span));

234: /// Evaluates an expression, coercing the values to strings.

237: /// quotes for string literals in `Expression`, so that we can decide whether
238: /// the expression is considered a bare string. The hack doesn't affect string
239: /// literals within lists or records. This function will remove the quotes
240: /// before evaluating the expression.
241: fn eval_argument(
242:     engine_state: &EngineState,
243:     stack: &mut Stack,
244:     expr: &Expression,
245:     spread: bool,
246: ) -> Result<Vec<String>, ShellError> {
247:     // Remove quotes from string literals.
248:     let mut expr = expr.clone();
249:     if let Expr::String(s) = &expr.expr {
250:         expr.expr = Expr::String(remove_quotes(s).into());

253:     let eval = get_eval_expression(engine_state);
254:     match eval(engine_state, stack, &expr)? {
255:         Value::List { vals, .. } => {
256:             if spread {
257:                 vals.into_iter()
258:                     .map(|val| val.coerce_into_string())

261:                 Err(ShellError::CannotPassListToExternal {
262:                     arg: String::from_utf8_lossy(engine_state.get_span_contents(expr.span)).into(),
263:                     span: expr.span,
264:                 })

266:         }
267:         value => {
268:             if spread {
269:                 Err(ShellError::CannotSpreadAsList { span: expr.span })
270:             } else {
271:                 Ok(vec![value.coerce_into_string()?])

273:         }

296: /// Performs glob expansion on `arg`. If the expansion found no matches or the pattern
297: /// is not a valid glob, then this returns the original string as the expansion result.

302:     let expanded_arg = if arg.starts_with('~') {
303:         expand_tilde(arg)

305:         arg.to_string()
306:     };

308:     if nu_glob::Pattern::new(&expanded_arg).is_err() {
309:         return Ok(vec![remove_inner_quotes(&expanded_arg).into_owned()]);
310:     }

312:     let options = nu_glob::MatchOptions {
313:         case_sensitive: true,
314:         require_literal_separator: false,
315:         require_literal_leading_dot: false,
316:         recursive_match_hidden_dir: true,
317:     };

319:     let Ok(paths) = nu_glob::glob_with_parent(&expanded_arg, options, cwd) else {
320:         return Ok(vec![remove_inner_quotes(&expanded_arg).into_owned()]);
321:     };

323:     let mut result = vec![];
324:     for path in paths {
325:         let path = path.map_err(|err| ShellError::IOErrorSpanned {
326:             msg: format!("{}: {:?}", err.path().display(), err.error()),
327:             span,
328:         })?;
329:         // Strip PWD from the resulting paths if possible.
330:         let path_stripped = path.strip_prefix(cwd).unwrap_or(&path);
331:         let path_string = path_stripped.to_string_lossy().to_string();

335:     let glob_match_count = result.len();
336:     if result.is_empty() {
337:         result.push(expanded_arg);
338:     }

340:     let mut finalized = Vec::with_capacity(result.len());
341:     for (index, path_string) in result.into_iter().enumerate() {
342:         let normalized = if index < glob_match_count {
343:             let expanded_dots = nu_path::dots::expand_dots(Path::new(&path_string));

346:                 path_string
347:             } else {
348:                 normalized
349:             }

351:             path_string
352:         };

354:         let cleaned = if !normalized.starts_with("--") {

382: /// Transforms `--option="value"` into `--option=value`. `value` can be quoted
383: /// with double quotes, single quotes, or backticks. Only removes the outermost
384: /// pair of quotes after the equal sign.
385: fn remove_inner_quotes(arg: &str) -> Cow<'_, str> {
386:     // Check that `arg` is a long option.
387:     if !arg.starts_with("--") {
388:         return Cow::Borrowed(arg);
389:     }
390:     // Split `arg` on the first `=`.
391:     let Some((option, value)) = arg.split_once('=') else {
392:         return Cow::Borrowed(arg);
393:     };
394:     // Check that `option` doesn't contain quotes.
395:     if option.contains('"') || option.contains('\'') || option.contains('`') {
396:         return Cow::Borrowed(arg);
397:     }
398:     // Remove the outermost pair of quotes from `value`.
399:     let value = remove_quotes(value);
400:     Cow::Owned(format!("{option}={value}"))

To be honest, the reason I didn't use nu_engine::glob_from() was that I couldn't understand what it's doing after reading its implementation several times. It doesn't seem to add much value compared to using nu_glob::glob_with_parent() directly.

part.text:
Fixed. The issue: in `expand_glob` (crates/nu-command/src/system/run_external.rs:330), a glob-expanded path equal to the cwd had `strip_prefix(cwd)` applied, producing an empty string that was passed to the external command — so `git add .` received `""` and git rejected it as an invalid pathspec.

**Fix** (crates/nu-command/src/system/run_external.rs:329-337): when stripping PWD from a matched glob path yields an empty string, fall back to `.` so the argument remains a valid path. Also added unit-test cases for `.` and `./` in `test_expand_glob`.

**Validation:**
- `cargo test -p nu-command system::run_external` — all unit tests pass
- End-to-end: `git add .` in nu now stages new files; `echo .` and `echo ./` print `.`
- `cargo test --test main` (1234 tests) and `cargo test -p nu-command` pass; the only two failures (`cd_permission_denied_folder`, `rm_prints_filenames_on_error`) were confirmed to fail on the unmodified baseline too (container runs as root)
